faq.q: How do I book a consultation?
faq.a: Use the Book a Consultation page to pick a time, or send the enquiry form on the Contact page. We reply to confirm.

faq.q: Do you work with individuals as well as businesses?
faq.a: Yes. We prepare individual tax returns and also handle business tax, GST and BAS, bookkeeping, payroll and company services.
Yes. Company registration and ASIC services are part of what we do, with corporate administration afterwards.

faq.q: I am not sure which service I need.
faq.a: Choose the closest one and describe your situation in the message. We will point you to the right service.

faq.q: What do I need to send first?
faq.a: Only your enquiry. Once we know the service, we tell you exactly which documents we need.

faq.q: Is anything lodged without my approval?
faq.a: No. We prepare the work and walk you through it. Nothing is lodged or filed until you have agreed.

faq.q: Can you help if I am behind on lodgements?
faq.a: Yes. Our tax compliance service covers catching up on overdue lodgements and responding to tax office correspondence.

posts.title: What to prepare before your first tax consultation
posts.excerpt: A short list of what to gather so your first meeting is quick and useful.
body: A first consultation goes faster when the basics are on the table. You do not need everything, but a little preparation means we can give you clear answers in the first meeting.
## Bring what shows your income
Gather the records that show what you earned during the year: income statements from employers, records of any business or freelance income, and details of interest, dividends or rental income.
## Bring what shows your costs
Collect receipts and records for expenses you think may be deductible. If you are unsure whether something counts, bring it anyway and we will tell you.
## Bring last year's return
A copy of your previous return helps us see what has changed and spot anything that was missed.
## Write down your questions
Note anything you want to ask: a new job, a property, a side business, or a letter from the tax office. It is easier to cover everything when it is written down.

posts.title: Bookkeeping habits that make tax time easier
posts.excerpt: Small weekly habits that save hours when returns and statements are due.
body: Most tax-time stress comes from records that were left to pile up. A few regular habits keep your books ready all year.
## Keep business and personal spending apart
A separate business account makes every transaction easier to sort and explain.
## Record transactions every week
Setting aside a fixed time each week to record income and expenses stops the backlog before it starts.
## Keep receipts as you go
Photograph or file receipts when you get them. A missing receipt is much harder to find months later.
## Reconcile regularly
Matching your records to your bank statements each month catches errors early, while they are still easy to fix.

posts.title: Sole trader or company: questions to ask before you register
posts.excerpt: The questions worth answering before you choose a business structure.
body: Choosing a structure is one of the first decisions in a new business, and it affects tax, paperwork and personal risk. These questions help frame the conversation.
## How much risk does the business carry?
Think about what could go wrong and who would be responsible. Structure affects whether business debts can reach your personal assets.
## How much admin are you ready for?
A company comes with more ongoing obligations, such as filings and records. Make sure you are ready for the extra work, or have someone to handle it.
## What are your plans for growth?
If you expect to take on partners, investors or staff, the right structure now can save a costly change later.
## Talk it through first
Every situation is different. A consultation before you register helps you choose with the full picture in front of you.
